archetype: Naya Dinosaur battlecruiser with two engines: an {5}{R}{G}{W} commander's combat-damage trigger, and a five-card enrage web that converts damage into draw, ramp, removal and tokens. strategic_frame.json calls it 'a linear critical-mass ramp deck' and the audit agrees by omission — no archetype keyword matched, so BASE targets applied and no aggro or combo override was used. Read every ratio target as a starting point, per the audit's own first note.
verdict: The deck functions early and interacts unusually well for a linear typal list: 89.4% turn-3 land drop, ramp assembled 93.9% at mean turn 2.044, 11 removal pieces inside an 18-card interactive suite, all five permanent classes covered. What limits it is the top end. Six of 65 nonland entries sit at mana value 8+ against a corpus average of ~1.5, the commander is one of them, and the deck's own goldfish puts mean available mana at 7.321 on turn 10. Two of the six discount themselves off a board — Blasphemous Act and Ghalta — so it is four of them, the commander among them, that compete for the one big-mana cast a seven-to-ten-turn game pays for. Colour compounds it: white and red sit at 20 sources each against a 36 target, 58% on curve. The enrage web is the healthier plan and is not commander-gated.

engine.declared: Two engines. Plan A is the commander's combat-damage trigger putting Dinosaurs onto the battlefield free; it needs eight mana and an unblocked hit. Plan B is a five-card enrage web that converts damage into draw, ramp, removal and tokens — and its triggers carry NO source restriction, so an opponent's attacker, blocker or damage-based removal fires them just as well; what the deck must supply itself is only the ability to fire the web PROACTIVELY, on its own terms, and it holds one free repeatable way to do that.

components.reading: Fourteen cards, 93.9% assembled at mean turn 2.044. Nothing to fix in the count; the failure is that 17 ramp pieces still leave mean available mana at 5.486 on turn 6.

Re-scoped from the audit's declared 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' group, which it sizes at 6 and measures at 67.3%. Reading all six oracle texts: Descendants' Path casts off the top of your library, Belbe's Portal and Monster Manual put a creature card from your HAND onto the battlefield, and Huatli's Roar chapter III searches a Dinosaur to hand — none can touch a card in the command zone. Only Otepec Huntmaster ('Dinosaur spells you cast cost {1} less') and Urza's Incubator ('Creature spells of the chosen type cost {2} less') reduce the cast the plan actually needs. A regex over all 89 maindeck entries for cost reduction returns no seventh candidate: Blasphemous Act, Ghalta and Flawless Maneuver reduce only themselves, and Etali, Pantlaza and Rishkar's Expertise cast free from exile, library and hand. At 2 copies, manabase.hypergeometric_at_least puts a reducer in hand 13.7% of openers and 24.7% by turn 6. The audit's own thinnest component is Blasphemous Act at size 1, but that is one half of a named combo target, not a class the main engine needs every game.

Seven cards, 73.7% assembled and 62.3% by turn 6. The 41.2% beside it in the audit is not a second measurement — it is the closed-form hypergeometric for a 7-of, the same arithmetic the redundancy citation's 41% comes from.

The five cards that actually convert damage: Ripjaw draws, Polyraptor copies itself, Ranging Raptors fetches a basic, Trapjaw Tyrant exiles an opponent's creature, Wrathful Raptors redirects the damage at any non-Dinosaur target. 60.8% assembled, 50.6% by turn 6. Temple Altisaur is the web's undeclared multiplier — it prevents all but 1 of any damage to your other Dinosaurs, and 1 damage still fires enrage.

Not a declared group, and that is the finding: no goldfish target pairs a converter with a source of damage, so the rate at which the web can be fired ON DEMAND has never been simulated. A regex over every maindeck oracle text returns exactly six cards that can deal damage to a creature you control. Four are one-shots (Blasphemous Act, Itzquinth's ETB, Triumphant Chomp, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard ability), Zacama's is repeatable at {2}{R} off a nine-mana body, and Forerunner of the Empire is the only free repeatable one. This constrains proactive ignition only — the enrage triggers themselves read 'Whenever this creature is dealt damage' with no source restriction, so combat damage and opponents' damage-based removal fire the web for free.

The declared connection kit: 62.2% assembled, 51.4% by turn 6. Two of the five are mislabelled for this job — the commander already reads 'Vigilance, trample, haste', so Regisaur Alpha's grant and Otepec Huntmaster's activation add nothing to HIS connection, though both matter enormously for the Dinosaurs he drops in.

The lowest measured rate of the six declared groups: 59.0% ever, 48.5% by turn 6. Flawless Maneuver is free only while you control a commander, and 5,533 of 10,000 goldfish iterations never cast him inside ten turns.

findings.note: Mechanical gate passes: `validate-diagnosis gishath` returns OK — 16 axes (5 weak), 6 cut / 4 add candidates, 5 open questions, measurements badged as data-derived and verdicts as coaching. No validator errors, so the substance review proceeded.

The replacement sentence — 'Closing two single points of failure with one card is what makes it worth settling, and the drawn game is what keeps it an open question rather than an add' — states a property of the card, not a rank. I ran a regex sweep for superlative markers (highest|best|most|only|unique|no other|nothing else|greatest|superior) over every string leaf of the document: open_questions[3] returns ZERO hits. The strings 'highest-value', 'in the pool' and 'the only candidate' are all absent from the file. The doctor's reported first-attempt replacement ('the only candidate in this document that closes two single points of failure') did not ship, explicitly or by implication: nothing in the field compares Marauding Raptor to the four add_candidates, to any pool, or to any unnamed set. The unenumerable superlative that failed iteration 2 is closed.

'Two single points of failure' is a count over a finite set the document itself publishes, and it is the correct count. engine.single_points_of_failure holds THREE entries: 'ignition', 'fodder', and 'Blasphemous Act (the one-sided apocalypse target)'. Marauding Raptor is named in fodder.closers. It closes ignition on oracle text — cards.csv gives 'Creature spells you cast cost {1} less to cast', and Gishath is a creature spell; CR 601.2f makes the commander tax an additional cost from which cost reductions are subtracted ('plus all additional costs and cost increases, and minus all cost reductions'), and CR 903.8 confirms the tax is an additional cost, so a creature-spell reduction does reach a cast from the command zone. It does NOT close the Blasphemous Act entry, whose closers list is empty. So the correct answer is two of three, and the document says two rather than rounding to 'all' — the count is checkable and checks out.

The clause that keeps it an open question rather than an add is exactly what stack 002 verified. 002-marauding-polyraptor-verdict.json has checker.verdict == pass (2 iterations, every step supported), its scenario extras state 'You control no sacrifice outlet and hold no instants' and flag both triggers as MANDATORY (no 'may'), and the checker confirms CR 732.1b (set of actions repeatable indefinitely = loop), CR 732.4 (loop of only mandatory actions = draw) and CR 104.4b (whole-table draw in a normal 3-player Commander game). 'Free repeatable ping' matches the oracle rider 'Whenever another creature you control enters, this creature deals 2 damage to it' — no mana cost, no once-per-turn. The question's own premise (a maindeck sacrifice outlet on the battlefield) is the precise escape the stack identifies, so the card is correctly withheld from add_candidates rather than prescribed.

Checked the surrounding block for a superlative smuggled in beside the fix, since that is where an unenumerable claim about Marauding Raptor would most naturally land. The 'only' constructions elsewhere in the document are all bounded and enumerated in place — engine.components[4] says Forerunner of the Empire is 'the only free repeatable one' out of a six-card list it prints, components[1] says 'no seventh candidate' after naming the six and the regex over all 89 maindeck entries, cut_candidates[5] says 'the only repeatable one besides Forerunner of the Empire' over the same six. Each ranks a set the reader can count inside the 99. None of them rank Marauding Raptor against anything outside the deck.
